A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCIF benchmark and contain complete main text, references, and Appendices A-F. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison; the localized caption overlap in v3 does not obscure essential evidence.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of 23 models, including benchmark scores in Tables 2, 9, and 10, modality ablations in Figure 2, and question-answering analyses in Figure 3.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark evaluations, modality ablations, question-answering analyses, and the model failure examples in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, fixed and mixed prompt procedures, model configurations, and inference procedures are unchanged. No algorithm or model component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same scientific-talk coverage, four languages, three modalities, 13 tasks, and short and long contexts. The 21 core talks, 220 question-answer pairs, and 100 summarization samples remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The 23-model roster and comparator membership in corresponding experiments are unchanged. Figure 3 still compares Qwen3, Phi4-Multimodal, Qwen2.5-VL, and Ola.

E3.justification: The prompt settings, context conditions, WER/COMET/BERTScore metrics, and generation settings are unchanged. Section 5.3 still evaluates MCIFmix long-form question answering with scores averaged across languages.

E4.justification: The prompt-variation comparison, modality ablation in Figure 2, question-type breakdown in Figure 3, and failure examples in Appendix F are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged: both present point estimates and language averages without reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 9, and 10 contain identical numerical entries, and Figures 2 and 3 retain the same plotted data. The reported findings and Appendix F failure outputs are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents a theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation contribution. The benchmark definitions are unchanged, with no added or revised formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty claims and contributions, including the findings concerning long contexts, prompt sensitivity, and multimodal integration.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning under-generation, language failures, weak modality integration, and question difficulty are unchanged. The single-turn, simple-instruction scope qualification and future-work discussion are also retained.

D1.justification: Annotation details, prompt lists, model weights and library versions, the 4096-token generation limit, GH200 hardware disclosure, and code/data access information are unchanged, including Appendices B-D.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, citations, and reference list are unchanged. MCIF's positioning relative to earlier benchmarks is retained.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes from v3, 19 February 2026, to v4, 10 August 2026. Body wording, headings, and section order are unchanged; Section 5.3 only reflows around Figure 3.

P2.justification: Figure 3 and its caption move upward beside the opening of Section 5.3, reflowing text across pages 9-10. This removes the caption's overlap with page number 9. Plot content, caption wording, and all other figures and tables remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 fixes the visible Figure 3 caption/page-number collision and removes the unnecessary narrow text wrapping at the start of page 10. This provides a limited readability improvement while preserving the scientific content and all appendix evidence.
